commands.cmd:
p=$(command -v mcporter) && v=$(mcporter --version) && echo "resolves: $p -> $(readlink -f "$p") | version: $v" && python3 -c "
import json, glob, sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts')
from host_receipts import pin_matches
v = sys.argv[1]
bp = [t['version'] for t in json.load(open('adoption/pins-linux-x86_64.json'))['tools'] if t['id'] == 'mcporter']
st = [x['version'] for x in json.load(open('manifests/stack.json'))['components'] if x['id'] == 'mcporter']
wp = sorted({w['pin'] for f in glob.glob('catalogs/landscape/*.json') for l in json.load(open(f)).get('layers', []) for w in (l.get('winners') or []) if w.get('component_id') == 'mcporter'})
print('bootstrap pin', bp, 'stack', st, 'winner pins', wp)
ok = bool(wp) and all(pin_matches(v, p) for p in wp) and bp == st == wp
print('pin_matches(version, winner pins):', ok)
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
" "$v"

claim: On host nativestack-5975wx-20260925 (WSL2 x86_64), MCPorter 0.13.13, the mcp-surfaces winner, bridges a real MCP server hermetically. With networking unshared (bwrap --unshare-net), it spawns a fresh QMD MCP stdio server isolated to a temporary HOME that holds a one-file fixture collection. It lists that server's tools (get, multi_get, query, status) and calls query twice with lexical search and rerank disabled. The query for the fixture's unique token returns the fixture file with the token in its snippet, and the query for an absent token returns 0 results. Calling a tool that does not exist exits non-zero with a JSON error naming that tool (positive control). The version and pin cross-check uses host_receipts.pin_matches. Every command exits 0 on its own assertions.
limitations: Supersedes the same-day receipt, whose query calls left QMD's default reranking on. That made QMD load a rerank model into the temporary HOME over the network on first run, which its limitations did not say (independent review of PR #277). This generation disables rerank and runs the server calls with networking unshared, so no model is fetched.
The bridged server is QMD 2.8.3 over stdio with a temporary lexical index; no production MCP server, no HTTP or OAuth transport and no host mcporter configuration file was used.

reviews.ref: Independent session review at catalog_revision 5b6014eb, worktree of branch claude/token-profile-receipts-20260925. REPRODUCE: re-ran cmd 1 (exit 0), cmd 2 verbatim under its own bwrap --unshare-net (exit 0) and cmd 3 (exit 1 plus JSON not-found error); all three output_sha256 values equal the recorded ones. SUPERSESSION REASON: accurate. Old and new cmd 1 and cmd 3 are byte-identical; new cmd 2 minus the bwrap wrapper minus the rerank:false argument equals old cmd 2 exactly; QMD 2.8.3 dist/mcp/server.js declares rerank default true and dist/llm.js DEFAULT_RERANK_MODEL is an hf: download. Control I ran: the receipt's own bwrap command with only rerank:false removed gives hit_exit=124 and assert_exit=1, so the old query form cannot pass without network. The citation 'PR #277' could not be checked offline (no local ref). ADEQUACY, use receipt, four points: (1) layer role PASS: mcp-surfaces requires bridging MCP servers and mcporter is its bridge winner; cmd 2 lists a spawned QMD stdio server's tools and calls query on a fixture, hit returns the file with the token in its snippet. (2) positive control PASS: absent-token query returns 0 results and a nonexistent tool exits 1 with a JSON error naming it; my control shows the assertion script fails when the hit does not arrive. (4) bound to winner PASS: component_id mcporter is a foundation.json mcp-surfaces winner; tool_versions 0.13.13 equals winner pin, stack version and adoption pin; cmd 1 prints pin_matches True and I ran pin_matches myself. (3) backed claims FAIL, this is the missing point: every sentence of the claim and the mcporter version and pin are backed by retained output, but limitation 2 carries two claims with no retained command. First, 'QMD 2.8.3' is a version claim and no retained command prints it (qmd --version does print 2.8.3 now, but that is my run, not the receipt's). Second, 'no host mcporter configuration file was used' is unbacked and not literally supported: I probed with a throwaway HOME holding an invalid ~/.mcporter/mcporter.json and mcporter list --stdio logged 'Ignoring config at ...: Failed to parse JSON', so mcporter loads its default config even for ad-hoc stdio, and the recorded run gave mcporter the real HOME (only the QMD server got a temporary HOME) while the host has a ~/.mcporter directory. FIX: retain a qmd --version command (or drop the version), and either run mcporter with an isolated HOME or --config in the recorded command, or reword the sentence to what the run shows (the bridged server was defined ad hoc, not from host config); then re-record as the next generation. Points 1, 2 and 4 and the supersession are otherwise fine.
